claims.claim: An observational study of 20,574 real coding-agent sessions across 1,639 repositories annotated each misalignment episode by form, cause, cost, and resolution and identified seven recurring forms.
claims.reason: Excerpt states 20,574 sessions from 1,639 repositories, annotation along form/cause/cost/resolution, and seven recurring forms.

claims.claim: In the field study, 90.50% of misalignment episodes impose effort and trust costs rather than irreversible system damage, yet 91.49% of visible resolutions still require explicit user correction.
claims.reason: Excerpt gives both figures verbatim: 90.50% effort/trust costs vs irreversible damage, 91.49% require explicit user correction.

claims.claim: While overall misalignment rates decline, the share of constraint violations and inaccurate self-reporting grows.
claims.reason: Excerpt states overall rates decline while constraint violations and inaccurate self-reporting grow in share.

claims.claim: A benchmark of 1,281 agent runs across more than 40 large repositories found that agents with only local tools begin to struggle systematically once a codebase exceeds roughly 400,000 lines of code, and that these failures stem from infrastructure limitations, not model intelligence.
claims.reason: Excerpt states 1,281 agent runs across 40+ repositories, local-tool agents struggle beyond ~400,000 LOC, and failures stem from infrastructure, not model intelligence.

claims.claim: On one refactoring task a baseline agent made 96 tool calls over 84 minutes with a 0.32 score, while an agent with better search infrastructure used 5 targeted search calls in 4.4 minutes achieving a 0.68 score.
claims.reason: Excerpt matches all figures: 96 calls/84 min/0.32 baseline vs 5 calls/4.4 min/0.68 with better search.
